data.description:
BUILDPLAN: S-2 — spike (§6). Time-boxed; **fails loudly rather than leaking into a feature build.**

Question it settles (verbatim): Does a `METHOD:REQUEST` invite render as **Accept/Decline** in Gmail, Outlook, and Apple Calendar — and does a `SEQUENCE+1` update *replace* the entry rather than duplicate it, and a `CANCEL` remove it? Neither Google nor Microsoft publishes a normative statement; this is the 15 minutes that separate R3 working from R3 looking like it works. **Runs as a standalone ~30-line script that hand-builds a `METHOD:REQUEST` + `SEQUENCE+1` + `CANCEL` triplet and sends it through Resend to the three inboxes — it needs no product code and can fire the moment `marquee@stage11.systems` is confirmed.**

Box: 1 h + operator inboxes. Blocks: **M-24** — the builder is written against the verdict, not the reverse. When: **D+2**, before any product code depends on the answer.
Human precondition (§8 item 6): three real inboxes — one Gmail (mandatory), one Outlook, one Apple Calendar — and a click on **Accept** in each. Needed within two hours of dispatch, not on Sunday afternoon.

ACs: — (de-risks AC-95, AC-97, AC-124; settles gate 10's shape)
Hours: 1
Workflow: fast-track
Shared files: none — standalone script; nothing merges into `src/` from here.
Deps: none
Plan: filled in by delegator's plan phase
data.title: Spike — ICS rendering in real mail clients

data.body: Review phase: working against forgejo/master @ bed8486d65220ef12539c65e4916313dc2dd9223; implementation commit 0ee0298d49c7545854834c532548470980396fa4.

data.reason: Inspect the delivered Gmail triplet for RSVP/update/cancel behavior, and provide Outlook plus Apple-backed inbox addresses to complete the client matrix.

data.body: Pre-PR rebase: working against forgejo/master @ 4f429473cc2de7a6d2d5cfaa73845cb005e589e1; final branch HEAD 23449743265813e8e86a835cb68cc15586930a72.
PR-base rebase: working against forgejo/master @ 12bf720447b887b094d67a60fc4a7bce9ab2e83e; current HEAD e67476e83e1d7a03a651a39bcad3ad760ab3de65.

Merged via auto-merge (PR #2, squash, 3ef7c647). Wire format + delivery verified; client-rendering half remains an operator oracle — needs_human stands with the inbox checklist. Review sha mismatch (2344974 vs head e67476e) resolved: identical tree hash b5d6c73, rebase-only.

S-2 oracle — deferred by operator 2026-08-10, with an agreed plan for closing it.

STATUS: the Gmail triplet has been sitting in benevolent.futures@gmail.com since 2026-08-09 06:21 UTC (search '[S-2 spike]'). Outlook and Apple rows were never sent — no addresses exist for them.

AGREED PLAN (operator, 2026-08-10): the orchestrator drives the GMAIL row itself via browser automation once this session is on the Alpha account — open the inbox in a browser surface and capture, as screenshots, (a) whether 1/3 renders Accept/Decline controls rather than a bare .ics attachment, and (b) whether 2/3 collapses onto 1/3 at 16:00 with no 15:00 duplicate. Screenshot evidence beats a verbal pass.

HARD BOUNDARY: do NOT click Accept without a fresh operator go-ahead — that writes to Atin's real Google Calendar. Reading the render is in scope; RSVPing is not. If the RSVP-then-update half cannot be proven without accepting, report that as the boundary rather than clicking.

STILL OPERATOR-ONLY: an Outlook.com address and an iCloud-backed address. Each is one run of 'node send.mjs <address>' from spikes/s2-ics-clients/ plus the same two-minute checklist in VERDICT.md.

CONSEQUENCE IF IT STAYS OPEN: MRQ-25 (calendar invites and the un-accept cascade) is written against this verdict. Building M-24 on an unverified assumption is exactly what the spike exists to prevent. Gmail alone is a defensible partial verdict for the competition; Outlook and Apple are the rows we would be guessing at.

data.note: Operator ruling 2026-08-12: not needed. The ICS client matrix does not require Outlook/Apple inbox addresses — the operator receives these in Gmail and considers that sufficient coverage.
